intro: DOCX to Markdown turns a Word document into clean, readable Markdown. It is the quick way to move a report, notes or documentation written in Word into a GitHub or GitLab repository, a wiki, a static site generator such as Hugo, Jekyll or MkDocs, or a notes app such as Obsidian.

Headings become hashes (#, ##…), bold and italics become asterisks, lists become dashes or numbers, links become [text](address) and simple tables become pipe tables. Tables with merged cells, which GitHub Markdown and CommonMark cannot express, are written as HTML; in pandoc's Markdown, as a grid table. Word formulas come out in LaTeX notation and footnotes stay as footnotes.

You can choose the flavor: GitHub's (GFM), the most widespread; CommonMark, the strict standard; or pandoc's Markdown, which supports more elements such as definition lists and table captions. Lines are not wrapped at a fixed width, so each paragraph stays on one line and changes read better in git.

Images can go in a media/ folder next to the .md, inside a ZIP; inside the Markdown itself as data, in a single file; or be left out with their alt text. The conversion runs with pandoc on our server, sandboxed, with up to 20 documents per batch.
steps: Choose the Markdown flavor and what to do with images.
Download the .md, or the ZIP with the .md and its images.

faq.q: Why do I get a ZIP instead of a .md?
faq.a: Because the document has images and you chose to keep them in a folder. The ZIP holds the .md and the media/ folder with the images, linked with relative paths. If you prefer a single file, choose “Inside the Markdown” or “No images”.

faq.q: Do images inside the Markdown show on GitHub?
faq.a: GitHub does not display images written as data (data:). For GitHub, the folder option is best: upload the .md and the media/ folder to the repository.

faq.q: Can I go back to Word later?
faq.a: Yes, with Markdown to DOCX. The round trip keeps the structure, though not the custom styles of the original document.
